survivingClaim: Precise obstruction, nothing about zeta zeros. PROVED (elementary, largely Gonek/classical): L1-L7 for the stage zeta_X = P_X + chi P_X(1-.): on-line form 2|P_X| cos Phi, stage zeros leave/join the line only through double zeros with Re D_X(1/2+it) = theta'(t), local index -sign(Phi_lambda Phi_tt), no event when sum_{p<=X} log p/(sqrt p - 1) < theta'(t). MEASURED (lane T = 8e3..1e9; referee T = 3e4, 3e5): at fixed a = log X/log T the stationary event has a positive rate close to the torus model; the Rouche inequality on Re s = 1/2 + c/log T fails at a height-independent positive fraction of sampled points for a = 0.5, c = 1, 2 (zeta about 0.6-1.0% and 0.1-0.25%; Davenport-Heilbronn about 1.3% and 0.6%, also height-independent); whole-window passes only at (a=0.25, c=4) and (a=0.1, c=8) for T >= 1e8 and right of 1. Phase-locking of stationary intervals to stage anti-points holds for zeta and for DH, not for random twists. The stage family gives no height-uniform inequality near the line and no step that fails for DH or the window translate.
obstruction: The prime-only exit event (double zero of the stage, Re D_X(1/2+it) = theta'(t)) is invariant under torus rotation and has a positive height-independent rate at fixed a = log X/log T (torus model followed to T = 1e20), so it carries no zero information. The Rouche inequality on Re s = 1/2 + c/log T fails at a height-independent positive fraction of sampled points for a = 0.5, c = 1, 2 (zeta 0.6-1.0% and 0.1-0.25%); whole-window passes occur only at (a=0.25, c=4) and (a=0.1, c=8) for T >= 1e8. The Davenport-Heilbronn two-character stage passes at comparable height-independent rates (1.3%, 0.6%) and tracks its off-line zeros: the comparison does not use the Euler product and gives box counts, not location. Measured in finite windows up to T = 1e9; nothing proved about rates.

lesson: The prime-only exit event of the Euler stage is invariant under torus rotation and has a positive height-independent rate at fixed log X/log T, so it cannot carry zero information. The Rouche comparison does not use the Euler product (the Davenport-Heilbronn two-character stage passes at the same rates and tracks its off-line zeros) and gives box counts, not location. Matching defect falls roughly like 1/a (0.05 spacings at a = 0.75) but no stage is exact. Ball products of ~1000 complex factors lose all precision by wrapping; sum logarithms instead.
followUp: Optional, low priority: test the anti-point sign law at X = T^0.75..T^1 over 1e5-1e6 zeros (no failure seen in three 2000-zero windows; rate below ~1e-3 unresolved) and whether its failures coincide with small zeta gaps. Controls not run: backward heat, sign twist, zeta(s+a)zeta(s-a), T-NR, Beurling, phase-rotated transfer operator, theta^w; Davenport-Heilbronn at one height only. No server units left running.
